tldr: Easing not yet liquid: Rate cuts delivered but money hasn't reached markets, liquidity still contracting.
Tech retreats: Semis down 14% in July, while banks and coal both up more than 10% — rotation in motion.
HK split: Fear fades, stocks climb, but strong dollar pushes money out of the currency peg.
What to do: Watch — don't chase.
summary: China easing stuck in pipes, tech pullback deepens, HK rebounds even as dollar drains the peg.
regime_read:
The mainland map reads Stagflation — growth is still weak but has stopped deteriorating, and inflation has warmed a little in the last week. Policy is in an awkward spot: the central bank has cut rates and the reserve requirement, yet system liquidity keeps contracting, so the easing has not reached the real economy yet. For the market, this means the growth scare isn't over, but the defensive and inflation-sensitive parts of the market are getting a bid. The dominant driver today is the tug-of-war between what the central bank is saying (easing) and what the money pipes are actually doing (draining).

The sector action fits the playbook of short-term mean reversion. Semiconductors and technology — the big winners of the past few months — have dropped hard, while banks, coal, consumer staples, and innovative drugs have surged. That is a classic handoff from extended growth names to beaten-down value and defensive groups. Hong Kong is running its own show: a fear unwind is lifting stocks even though the strong dollar is pushing the currency peg to the weak side, meaning capital is leaving. That split matters — a sustained dollar rally would eventually cap Hong Kong's gains.
conflicts: Easing vs liquidity: The central bank is cutting rates, but the money pipes show contracting liquidity — easing hasn't taken hold.
HK stocks vs peg: Hong Kong equities are rising on fading fear, yet the dollar strength is still pulling money out of the peg.
Regime signals split: The growth score says weak, but factory output and breadth data aren't nearly as dire.
rotation_check: The mean-reversion pattern is clear: hot tech rolls over, cool defensives and banks step up — exactly the short-term handoff the playbook expects.
transmission: If the dollar keeps strengthening, Hong Kong's stock rebound will face headwinds from sustained capital outflows.
If rate cuts finally turn system liquidity expansive, brokers and property should be the first to lead.
watch_items: PBOC pumps liquidity: If the central bank's actions start expanding system money, the whole tone shifts.
Yuan pressure: If USD/CNY breaks higher, Hong Kong peg strain intensifies and caps the rebound.
July 31 PMI: A surprise pickup in manufacturing could nudge the map from Stagflation toward something better.
Tech stops bleeding: If semis stop falling, the rotation may be done and new leaders could emerge.

zh.summary: 中国宽松政策传导受阻，科技股回调加深，香港反弹，尽管美元正在抽离联系汇率。
zh.regime_read:
中国大陆图景显示滞胀——增长仍然疲弱但已停止恶化，且过去一周通胀略有升温。政策处于尴尬境地：央行已降息并下调存款准备金率，但系统性流动性持续收缩，因此宽松政策尚未传导至实体经济。对市场而言，这意味着增长恐慌尚未结束，但防御性和通胀敏感板块正获得买盘。今日主导因素是央行所言（宽松）与资金管道实际所为（抽水）之间的拉锯。

板块表现符合短期均值回归剧本。半导体和科技股——过去几个月的大赢家——大幅下挫，而银行、煤炭、必需消费品和创新药大涨。这是从涨幅已高的成长股转向超跌价值股和防御板块的经典切换。香港则独立行情：恐慌情绪消退推高股市，尽管强势美元将联系汇率推向弱方，这意味着资本正在流出。这种分化很重要——持续的美元上涨最终将限制香港的涨幅。
zh.rotation_check: 均值回归模式清晰：热门科技股熄火，冷门防御股和银行股接棒——正是剧本预期的短期切换。
tldr: 宽松尚未传导：降息已实施，但资金未流入市场，流动性仍在收缩。
科技股回落：半导体板块7月下跌14%，而银行和煤炭均涨超10%——板块轮动正在进行。
香港分化：恐慌消退，股市走高，但强美元推动资金流出联系汇率制度。
conflicts: 宽松 vs 流动性：央行正在降息，但资金管道显示流动性收缩——宽松尚未生效。
港股 vs 联系汇率：香港股市因恐慌消退而上涨，但美元强势仍在将资金抽离联系汇率。
机制信号分化：增长得分显示疲弱，但工厂产出和广度数据远没有那么糟糕。
transmission: 如果美元持续走强，香港股市的反弹将面临持续资本外流的压力。
如果降息最终使系统流动性变得宽松，券商和房地产应率先引领。
watch_items: 中国央行注入流动性：如果央行的行动开始扩大系统货币，整体基调将发生转变。
人民币压力：如果美元兑人民币突破上行，香港联系汇率制度压力加剧并限制反弹。
7月31日PMI：制造业的意外回升可能将格局从滞胀转向更好的方向。
科技股止血：如果半导体停止下跌，板块轮动可能已完成，新的领涨者可能浮现。
